text:
Anaheim arrives with momentum and a thin lineup. The Ducks came back from three goals down to beat Ottawa 6-3 on Sunday, with Cutter Gauthier scoring three, and they are 2-2-1 in their last five without A.J. Greer and Ryan Poehling. Roger McQueen has taken Poehling's spot beside Nesterenko and Killorn. Vancouver, off a 4-2 loss to Toronto, is 1-4-0 in its last five and missing Filip Chytil, with Elias Pettersson now beside Lekkerimäki and Boeser. The Canucks did win the last meeting 6-5 in overtime on Oct 27.

Neither team has controlled play. At five on five, ANA has taken 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and VAN 40%. Vancouver gives up 3.91 expected goals per 60, and Anaheim keeps taking penalties, 4.79 a game. The goalie picture favors the Ducks on paper: projected starter Laurent Brossoit is at -0.07 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with what his shots suggested), while Kevin Lankinen is at -12.25 this season and -20.31 last.

Gauthier is 45% to score and 71% for a point. Leo Carlsson is 81% for a point, and Jeff Paterson of Rink Wide posted that Filip Hronek is a top-15 scorer among defencemen with a five-game point streak.

Our under-the-radar picks: Judd Caulfield, a third-liner whose shots have been dangerous lately (22% to score), and Mikael Granlund, 65% for a point, as players to watch.
